question: Should `2026.7.1-2` become the Windows setup last-known-good gateway version despite reported `2026.7.1` startup failures, based on current-head Windows/WSL acceptance evidence?
rationale: The code path is intentionally centralized and requires no design change, but the semantic LKG designation is a release-quality judgment that source review cannot establish.

options.title: Accept after targeted acceptance proof
options.body: Run and review the current-head fresh setup, gateway health, pairing, existing-distro repair, rollback, build, and required test evidence, then merge if the upstream failure disposition is satisfactory.

options.title: Retain the prior LKG
options.body: Keep `2026.6.11` pinned until `2026.7.1-2` has sufficient supported-path acceptance evidence.

recommendation.title: Accept after targeted acceptance proof
recommendation.body: Run and review the current-head fresh setup, gateway health, pairing, existing-distro repair, rollback, build, and required test evidence, then merge if the upstream failure disposition is satisfactory.
